statistics.locator: Results, paragraph on the after-effect phase (page 3, right after the adaptation-phase ANOVA)
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
within_factors: Episode (5 levels, episodes 21–25 of the after-effect phase; inferred from F(4,88))
statistics.model_fitted_to: median initial pointing direction error per 50-s episode for each subject
statistics.admissible_reason: Main effect of the within-subject factor Episode, not a between-group contrast; numerator df > 1.
statistics.notes: This is the within-factor Episode effect from the after-effect-phase ANOVA (between-factor Age, within-factor Episode). No Age main effect is printed for this phase.

statistics.locator: Results, paragraph on the after-effect phase (page 3)
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
within_factors: Episode (5 levels, episodes 21–25 of the after-effect phase; inferred from F(4,88))
statistics.model_fitted_to: median initial pointing direction error per 50-s episode for each subject
statistics.direction_quote: indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term (Age × Episode), not a between-group contrast on the after-effect; numerator df > 1.
statistics.notes: The quoted sentence about the young group declining faster describes the shape of the interaction over episodes, not which group had the larger after-effect magnitude.

statistics.effect_as_written: Age (main effect) in the after-effect phase
statistics.admissible_reason: No between-group (Age) statistic for the after-effect phase is printed on these pages.
statistics.notes: For the after-effect phase the paper reports only Episode and the interaction; the Age main effect is not given numerically. The text states verbally: "when visual feedback was removed after adaptation, the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups" — no test statistic accompanies this. No statistic for episode 21 alone is reported either.

statistics.admissible_reason: No standardised effect size is printed for the after-effect phase.
statistics.notes: These pages print only F values with bounded p values (and one t test for the trail-making test); no d, g or eta-squared values appear anywhere.

parsed.notes: Only one ANOVA on the after-effect phase is reported (between-factor Age, within-factor Episode, F df of 4,88 implying 5 after-effect episodes). It prints Episode and the Age × Episode interaction; the Age main effect is described verbally as similar in both groups but no statistic is given. Other statistics on page 3 concern different outcomes and are therefore not transcribed here: the adaptation-phase ANOVA (Age F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05; Episode F(14,308)=41.14; interaction F(14,308)=3.44), the refresh-phase ANOVAs (Age F(1,22)=13.42; Episode F(2,44)=6.18; and episodes 20 vs 26: Age F(1,22)=13.78, Episode F(1,22)=7.79), the tracking transfer ANOVA (Procedure F(1,43)=144.09), and the trail-making test t(22)=5.25. Means/SDs for after-effect episodes are shown only graphically in Fig. 1, which is not available as text.
